one_sentence: The Great Inversion argues that Western culture has systematically relabeled decoherence as freedom and coherence as oppression, driven by entropy's neurochemical rewards.
executive_summary: This document argues that Western civilization has undergone a systematic inversion of values, where coherence (structure, truth, boundaries) is rebranded as oppression and decoherence (entropy, relativism, dissolution) is rebranded as liberation. It identifies four mechanisms: the dopamine hijack (rewarding constraint removal), the autonomy illusion (mistaking entropy for freedom), the relativism cascade (collapsing truth into noise), and the accusation reversal (attacking coherence as harmful). The conclusion is that this inversion is a civilization-scale increase in entropy, disguised as moral progress, and that only external coherence input—negentropy or grace—can reverse it. The document uses physics (Second Law, entropy) and theology (Isaiah, Matthew) to diagnose the phenomenon.
short_summary: This document is a deep-dive analysis of the cultural inversion where decoherence is celebrated as freedom and coherence is condemned as oppression. The core structural claim is that this inversion is a civilization-scale entropy increase driven by neurochemical rewards for constraint removal. Key evidence includes four mechanisms (dopamine hijack, autonomy illusion, relativism cascade, accusation reversal) and measurable declines in human flourishing metrics. It matters because it provides a physics-based diagnosis of cultural decay and identifies the only remedy as external coherence input (negentropy/grace).
